On Thu, Nov 4, 2021 at 5:06 PM Justin Goes <[jgoes@paytrace.com|mailto:jgoes@paytrace.com]> wrote:


{quote}Michael and team – thanks so much for your time today.

 

A couple follow up questions after reviewing some material after our call.

 

In the integration method we discussed, it looks like PayTrace will not be in control of settlement. We can initiate settlement/batch close, but it is EPX that would be creating the batch file being sent off for processing. So the transactions are kept at the host, and then the host/EPX settles. I am curious to better understand if you have an integration option that would allow PayTrace to create and send you the formatted settlement file? The reason I ask, is that this is where PayTrace brings a lot of value to the table with our experience around building settlement files to optimize interchange. For example, if there are downgrade issues, we can work internally to fix and correct those issues when we control the creation of the settlement file. If we were to pursue the path we discussed this morning, we would be dependent on EPX to help identify, resolve and validate reasons for downgrades. I am not suggesting that we would deviate from the path we discussed on the call today, however I am just curious of there is an integration method where PayTrace can format the settlement file and provide it to EPX when closing the batch?{quote}

I am hoping we have a syntax problem.  First, there is no way that we would allow an edited settlement file, so I am assuming you are talking about a capture file.  If you want to edit the capture file that is not a problem, however, if the format is invalid or out of balance it would be rejected and miss the funding cycle. The way EPX works is we rate interchange at the time of settlement and then EPX advantage will take qualifying transactions and perform L2 or L3 repair (L3 is not in production, scheduled for late November).  The reason we know the difference between repaired and non-repaired is because of this process. 




If you send us a qualified L3 transaction we will not try to repair it and would not be able to give you the non-repaired interchange amount.  Today we process L3 transactions for customers without issue. 

{quote}
As a follow up to the above question, how confident is EPX in its ability to qualify L3 transactions? How often do you run into downgrade issues with gateways leveraging the integration method we talked about today? Are they typically a result of bad data the gateway is providing, or is it a result of how the settlement file is generated and submitted?{quote}

As I said we are currently in development and testing at this time. Normally other gateways pass L3 transactions which rarely if ever downgrade.  

{quote}

What happens when we submit a batch close request, and the host (EPX) and PayTrace are out of balance? Do we get a rejected batch notification and have to work through the discrepancy?{quote}

Yes as I said above.  

{quote}

I forgot to mention that we are interested in learning about how we can onboard merchant accounts with NAB/EPX. Do you all have a merchant onboarding API that would allows us to send through merchant applications and do the vetting/risk analysis/underwriting and MID generation? If so, could you send us a link to that?{quote}

I believe Bryan Long sent you this information.  

{quote}

For getting access to the deposit information, I recall that we would have to go and retrieve a file with that information at some interval/daily. What does the communication look like for this. Is it a SFTP transfer? Is it done over a VPN?{quote}

There a number of ways to access this information: STFP, or VIA a DataLake private partition that would require you to have a Snowflake License.  

{quote}{quote}

We were able to confirm that our Payanywhere hardware terminals cannot be used with USAePay... so for a Payanywhere integration, the merchant (Zerorez) would proceed to process payments through us instead.

Regarding your inquiry about launching the Payanywhere (PA) Mobile SDK from a browser app instead of a mobile app, the PA Mobile SDK is not supported by being launched from a browser app.

Since your preference is to process card-present payments via a terminal/device, the PA Mobile SDK is the solution for that.
Developer portal integration guide: https://developer.paymentshub.com/products/card-present/mobile-sdks/pa-mobile-sdk/android-integration
If you were to build out the Android app integration with our PA Mobile SDK, the Zerorez technicians could use the mobile app (instead of loading the current browser app) to take card-present payments via the BBPOS card reader device.
If you are needing to streamline the record keeping aspect, in addition to handling the payment response in real-time within the mobile app, you can also configure it to send the current transaction response data to a URL of your choosing, using a webhook setup. You can use the webhook to fulfill the need to pass data to another system. 
For example, you could send each transaction response to the URL of a page associated with Zerorez’s browser CRM app, and then handle that data however you like (including sending the responses to a database, for example). It’s important to note that this programmatic task, which sends transaction responses to the specified URL using the webhook, is not part of the customer-facing flow or the user experience - the task just runs on the backend.

ISV-Notes:
 This partner works with payments for phone bills and for prepaid phone cards.  They require 3D Secure v2.  They are currently on authorize.net which I've been advised only supports v1, so they are moving to a direct to EPX integration.
From their process description, they are very much in-scope with their current system.  It seemed like they want to stay that way.
They have a portal, which is used by stores to buy/resell their product.  For instance, the store might buy $1000 of the product and then resell it in $20 or $50 increments to customers.
They also either have or are building an app, for end customers to use.  The app and also portal allow customers to sign up for their automatic recharge functionality which works like such: if someone is using their prepaid phone card, and the balance drops below $3 or so, then the card on file is automatically charged at that time to add more funds to the card.  The app and portal also allow the user to pay bills (including other people's bills in 140+ countries).  They may refer to this as either 'domestic top-up' or 'international top-up'.
The partner confirmed that all requests to us would be coming from their server(s).  They would not be coming from the mobile app itself.  So I believe either server post or EPI would be feasible from a technical standpoint, at least once EPI gets those few extra fields added which I was recently advised should be added within a couple weeks.  
There are still a couple outstanding questions as to:
 - what the 3D secure flow is from a mobile app (is it the same as the flow from a site?)
 - can any type of mobile app use 3d secure, or does it have to be a certain type?  I know that some apps get weird or the user experience goes bad when it comes to redirecting a user from the app to a web page."
